blocks.text: SSL/TLS Inspection policies allow you to inspect traffic sent using the secure HTTPS protocol to ensure that it is, in fact, encrypted and fully secure and is not exploited to deliver security threats. Zscaler inspects SSL/TLS traffic by establishing a separate SSL tunnel between the user's browser and the destination server.
After you have set up URL Filtering options, review the following SSL/TLS Inspection policies:

blocks.item: Under Exempted Categories, review the categories that Zscaler exempts from SSL/TLS inspection. These categories (Healthcare and Finance) are not inspected because they might contain a user's personally identifiable information (PII).

blocks.text: By default, Zscaler inspects SSL/TLS traffic from Microsoft's web-based applications such as OneDrive. If you want to use Microsoft's recommended setting, which exempts that traffic from SSL/TLS inspection, click Advanced SSL Settings, select M365 Exempted, and click Save.

blocks.item: Under All Users, All Other Destinations, note that categories that are not exempted have their SSL/TLS traffic inspected.
Under SSL Root Certificate, Zscaler's intermediate root certificate is installed. You can select your own certificate later in the Zscaler Admin Console.
When you are done reviewing the SSL/TLS Inspection policies, click Next to move on to review the cyber threat protection policies.

blocks.text: Zscaler installs its recommended SSL/TLS Inspection policies by default. You can fine-tune these policies later in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see Configuring SSL/TLS Inspection Policy.
